Add marginal histogram or density overlay

Source: R/fmt_plot.R
fmt_his.Rd

Overlays a rescaled histogram or density curve on the existing plot, using the x-axis variable (or a user-supplied variable).

Usage

fmt_his(
  plot,
  type = c("histogram", "density", "h", "d"),
  height_ratio = 0.3,
  data = NULL,
  con_var = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot, patchwork, or list of ggplots.

type

"histogram" (or "h") or "density" (or "d").

height_ratio

Finite number from 0 to 1 giving the fraction of each visible panel's y-axis range used for the overlay height. Default: 0.3.

data

Optional data frame, layer data function or formula. If NULL, uses the plot data or the first applicable layer's data.

con_var

Optional single column name overriding the x mapping. If NULL, retains the plot's x-mapping expression, falling back to the first applicable layer mapping.

...

Named overlay controls. Unknown, unnamed or duplicate arguments are rejected. NULL retains the default for each control.

binwidth

Positive finite bin width or a function, as in ggplot2::geom_histogram(). Default: 3. Histogram only; measured after the x-scale transformation.

adjust

Positive finite density bandwidth multiplier. Default: 3. Density only.

his_color

Single colour or NA. Default: "gray85".

his_alpha

Finite opacity from 0 to 1. Default: 0.5.

y_rescale

Two finite values giving the baseline and peak in original y-data units. Default: the panel bottom and height_ratio above it in transformed display coordinates.

ylim

Two y-coordinate limits in original data units. NA endpoints remain automatic. Default: original limits; original coordinate type, expansion, clipping and aspect ratio are retained.

Value

Same type as input.

Details

Counts and densities are scaled from statistical zero, preserving their relative heights. The fill starts at the requested baseline. Each facet is scaled independently; distribution layers do not retrain the original position scales or inherit grouping, weights or legends. Cartesian coordinates, including flipped and fixed-ratio coordinates, are supported. Nested patchwork layouts and annotations are preserved; spacers, wrapped grobs and inset overlays are skipped. Repeated calls add additional distribution layers. Mapping expressions and data callbacks are evaluated during the normal plot build; formatting does not build or refit the original plot.

See also

Other plot formatting: fmt_axis(), fmt_axisText(), fmt_axisTile(), fmt_bg(), fmt_boxplot(), fmt_com(), fmt_expand(), fmt_legend(), fmt_panel(), fmt_plot(), fmt_plot_base(), fmt_point(), fmt_raster(), fmt_ref(), fmt_scale(), fmt_strip(), fmt_strip2(), fmt_tag(), fmt_text()

Examples

library(ggplot2)
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(100), y = rnorm(100))
p <- ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) + geom_point()
fmt_his(p, type = "histogram", height_ratio = 0.3, binwidth = 0.5)

fmt_his(p, type = "density", height_ratio = 0.2, adjust = 1)
